FATHER_OF|per_er|per_zarah.reason: Gen.38.6 names Tamar as Er's wife, and Gen.38.27-30 says Tamar bore twins, one named Zarah, but none of the verses says whose child Zarah is, so they neither state nor contradict that Er is his father.

FATHER_OF|per_esau|per_amalek_gen_36_16.reason: Gen.36.16 lists Amalek among the dukes "that came of Eliphaz," and Gen.36.10 names Eliphaz as the son of Adah and Esau, so the verses point to Eliphaz as Amalek's parent rather than Esau directly.

FATHER_OF|per_lamech_gen_4_18|per_jabal.reason: Gen.4.19 names Adah as one of Lamech's wives and Gen.4.20 says "Adah bare Jabal," so the verses make Lamech the father of Jabal through his wife Adah.

FATHER_OF|per_lamech_gen_4_18|per_jubal.reason: Gen 4:21 says only that Jubal was Jabal's brother, and Gen 4:19-20 names Lamech's wives Adah and Zillah and says Adah bore Jabal, but no verse says who bore Jubal or who fathered him, so the verses neither state nor rule out Lamech as Jubal's father.

FATHER_OF|per_lamech_gen_4_18|per_naamah.reason: Gen 4:22 only says Naamah was the sister of Tubalcain, whose mother is Zillah, and Gen 4:19 names Lamech as Zillah's husband, but neither verse names Naamah's mother or father, so Naamah could be a half-sister through Adah or a child of another man, and the verses do not establish Lamech as her father.

FATHER_OF|per_lamech_gen_4_18|per_tubalc.reason: Gen.4.19 names Zillah as one of Lamech's wives, and Gen.4.22 says "Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain," with no other father named, which makes Lamech the father plain.

FATHER_OF|per_seir|per_timna.reason: Verse 22 says only that Timna is Lotan's sister, and verse 20 names Seir as Lotan's father, but no verse names Timna's parent, and a sister could be a half-sibling with a different father, so the verses do not settle whether Seir is Timna's father.

FATHER_OF|per_terah|per_sarah.reason: Gen.20.12 has Abraham say Sarah is "the daughter of my father," and Gen.11.26-27 names Terah as the father who begat Abram, so Terah is Sarah's father (the mother is not named, which does not affect the father link).

MOTHER_OF|per_adah_gen_4_19|per_jubal.reason: Gen.4.20 says Adah bare Jabal, and Gen.4.21 only calls Jubal Jabal's brother without naming his mother, so the verses do not show whether Adah or another wife bore Jubal, since they could be half-siblings.

MOTHER_OF|per_eve|per_seth.reason: Gen.4.25 says "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth," and Gen.3.20 names Adam's wife as Eve ("Adam called his wife's name Eve"), so the verses make Eve Seth's mother.

MOTHER_OF|per_milcah|per_laban_gen_29_5.reason: Gen 22:20 and 22:23 say Milcah bore children to Nahor, and Gen 29:5 calls Laban Nahor's son, but no given verse names Laban among Milcah's children, the eight named in 22:23 are not listed in the provided text, and Gen 22:24 (not provided) mentions a concubine, Reumah, who also bore Nahor sons.

MOTHER_OF|per_shuah_gen_38_2|per_zerah_g.reason: Gen.46.12 names Zerah only as a son of Judah, and Gen.38.2 and 38.12 show Judah's wife Shuah but never say she bore Zerah or any other child, so the given verses neither state the link nor point to a different mother.

MOTHER_OF|per_zillah|per_naamah.reason: The verse says Zillah bare Tubalcain and that Naamah was his sister, but it never says Zillah bore Naamah, and "sister" could be a half-sibling with a different mother.
